title: What is TypeScript?
overview: TypeScript is a programming language developed by Microsoft that is built on top of JavaScript. It adds static typing features to JavaScript, which helps developers catch errors early and write more reliable code.

title: Why Do We Use TypeScript?
overview: TypeScript improves JavaScript development by providing type checking, better code suggestions, and easier code maintenance, especially in large applications.

example.title: Benefits of TypeScript
example.content:
✔ Finds errors before running code
✔ Better autocomplete
✔ Improves code readability
✔ Helps maintain large projects

title: JavaScript vs TypeScript
overview: JavaScript is dynamically typed, while TypeScript adds static typing. TypeScript code is converted into JavaScript before execution.

example.title: Comparison

title: How TypeScript Works
overview: TypeScript code cannot run directly in browsers or React Native. It is first compiled into JavaScript using the TypeScript compiler.

example.title: TypeScript Flow
example.content:
TypeScript Code
        ↓
TypeScript Compiler
        ↓
JavaScript Code
        ↓
Application

title: TypeScript in React Native
overview: TypeScript is widely used in React Native applications to provide type safety for components, props, navigation, API responses, and application logic.

example.title: React Native Type Example

title: Topic Summary
overview: You learned what TypeScript is, why it is used, how it differs from JavaScript, how it works, and why it is useful in React Native development.
